# Project instructions

## Project context

- This is a Unity 6 project using C#. The exact editor version is in [ProjectVersion.txt](../ProjectSettings/ProjectVersion.txt).
- [Mirror](../Assets/Mirror/version.txt) is the installed networking framework.
- [FizzySteamworks](../Assets/Mirror/Transports/FizzySteamworks/README.md) is installed as a Mirror transport for Steam networking.
- Steamworks.NET provides Steamworks API bindings and is installed through the Unity Package Manager Git dependency in [manifest.json](../Packages/manifest.json); its resolved revision is in [packages-lock.json](../Packages/packages-lock.json).
- The game is 2.5D: environments are 3D, while characters use 2D world sprites. The local player's first-person sprites belong to a UI canvas; other players see that character's world sprites.
- [steam_appid.txt](../steam_appid.txt) contains Spacewar's temporary App ID `480` for development. Use the project's own App ID for release; standalone Steam playtests need the file beside the executable.

## Working with the project

- For Steam multiplayer, use the existing Mirror, FizzySteamworks, and Steamworks.NET stack by default. Do not replace these libraries or add alternative networking or Steam packages without the user's approval.
- Before making networking changes, inspect the relevant scripts, scenes, prefabs, NetworkManager, transport assignment, and Steam initialization. Installed packages do not imply that these are configured or working.
- Check the installed package versions and the FizzySteamworks README when choosing APIs or explaining setup. Describe any required Unity Inspector, Steam client, and testing steps, and distinguish unverified behavior from verified results.
- Prefer project code over edits to third-party Mirror or FizzySteamworks sources unless those edits are necessary. Preserve Unity `.meta` files, GUIDs, and serialized references when moving or renaming assets.

## Player foundation

- [NetworkPlayer.prefab](../Assets/PREFABS/NetworkPlayer.prefab) separates owner-only camera/UI from remote world sprites through [PlayerPresentation](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Player/PlayerPresentation.cs). World sprites animate through SpriteRenderer, not Animator.
- [PlayerMovement](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Player/PlayerMovement.cs) uses a CharacterController and the Vector2 `Player/Movement` input action with WASD and a Shift sprint (see Player HUD, health and stamina). Only Mirror's local player reads input; its root transform uses client-to-server synchronization for this basic prototype, not server-validated movement.
- [SampleScene](../Assets/Scenes/SampleScene.unity) contains [SteamNetworkManager](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Player/SteamNetworkManager.cs) (a Mirror NetworkManager), NetworkManagerHUD, and FizzySteamworks (SteamSockets). The player prefab is assigned for automatic spawning, with six connections total (host plus five guests). No separate scene camera/audio listener is present.
- [PlayerLook](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Player/PlayerLook.cs) uses the existing Vector2 `Player/Look` pointer-delta binding from the Keyboard&Mouse group, cloned for the local player only. Mouse sensitivity is degrees per pixel (no deltaTime multiplier). Horizontal look rotates the networked player root before movement/interaction; pitch stays on the owner's camera and is limited to +/-85 degrees by default. Existing PlayerVision synchronization picks up camera yaw.
- Mouse capture starts on local spawn. Escape toggles capture for HUD access; focus loss releases it until Escape is pressed again. Steam Overlay temporarily releases capture and pauses look; returning to gameplay discards the first frame of mouse motion. Disabling or despawning the local player releases the cursor.
- [PlayerSpawnPoints](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Level/PlayerSpawnPoints.cs) (in `Capstone.Level`) on the scene's SpawnPoints parent registers its active direct children as Mirror start positions when enabled and unregisters them when disabled. Six children are provided, selected in round-robin order. Add/move spawn children in the Editor before starting a session.
- [Player tests](../Assets/Tests/PlayMode/NetworkPlayerTests.cs) run in the Unity Test Runner's PlayMode with no active NetworkManager. They use an in-memory host connection, not Steam, to check prefab wiring, WASD/diagonal movement, and owner/remote visibility.

## Player HUD, health and stamina

- [PlayerHealth](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Player/PlayerHealth.cs) on NetworkPlayer has six health, synchronized by server-to-client SyncVars. Server gameplay calls `TakeDamage(positiveAmount, sourceIdentity = null)` and `Heal(positiveAmount)`; values clamp to 0..6. Pass the attacker's NetworkIdentity so the fatal hit records `KillerAssetId` (its prefab asset id) for the death screen; `IsDead` is health 0. There is no client damage Command or automatic healing. New player spawns start at six; the persistent HUD does not persist health across respawns.
- [PlayerHud](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Player/PlayerHud.cs) is a separate Screen Space Overlay [prefab](../Assets/PREFABS/PlayerHud.prefab), placed as a root in SampleScene, not inside NetworkPlayer. It persists via DontDestroyOnLoad, rejects duplicates, binds only to NetworkClient.localPlayer, and hides its panels while no local player exists. Disabling/re-enabling, player replacement and reconnects rebind the UI. Add future local player readouts to this HUD rather than to the player prefab.
- Assign Full Heart, Half Heart and Empty Heart on the HUD component in its prefab; heart slots are left-to-right, two health each (5 = full/full/half, 4 = full/full/empty). Unassigned heart sprites intentionally render nothing. Assign a background Sprite on HealthPanel's Image, set its tint to white for original artwork, and adjust size/anchors as desired. UI Images do not intercept clicks. The existing first-person canvas remains separate and unchanged.
- [PlayerStamina](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Player/PlayerStamina.cs) on NetworkPlayer has 100 maximum stamina in client-to-server SyncVars: the owning client simulates it (like movement) and Mirror relays it to everyone; it is not server-validated. Sprint drains 15/s, regeneration is 10/s after a 0.8 s delay since the last use, and reaching 0 locks every stamina action until 30% refills. Future owner actions (e.g. attacks) call `TryUseStamina(amount)`, which returns false while exhausted or while travel is in progress.
- `Player/Sprint` is a Button bound to `<Keyboard>/shift` (either Shift). [PlayerMovement](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Player/PlayerMovement.cs) sprints at **Sprint Multiplier** (1.5x) only while Shift is held, movement input exists, stamina allows it, and the player actually moves; standing still with Shift never drains. PlayerVision publishes Run while sprinting when the CharacterDefinition's Run frames are ready, otherwise Walk.
- The HUD's StaminaPanel (background sprite) holds StaminaFill, a Filled/Horizontal/Left Image whose fill amount follows the local player's stamina. Below **Low Stamina Fraction** (30%; exactly 30% does not blink), without complete depletion, only the fill's alpha blinks at **Blinks Per Second** down to **Blink Minimum Alpha**. After complete depletion (`PlayerStamina.IsExhausted`), the whole bar (panel background and fill) blinks until stamina recovers to the 30% threshold, then the background alpha is restored. Filled Images need a sprite assigned.
- [PlayerSprintFov](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Player/PlayerSprintFov.cs) on PlayerCamera eases the owner's FOV out by **FOV Increase** (6 degrees) at **Transition Speed** while sprinting and removes only its own offset afterwards, coordinating with PlayerFearEffects so panic shudder restoration stays correct. NetworkPlayerTests cover Shift sprint speed/drain, regen delay, exhaustion lockout, sync and FOV.
- The HUD's last child **DamageFlash** (stretched nested Canvas, sorting order 500, non-raycast red Image) runs [PlayerDamageFlash](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Player/PlayerDamageFlash.cs): whenever the local player's health drops it jumps to **Peak Alpha** (0.6), holds **Hold Seconds** (0.08) and fades over **Fade Seconds** (0.6). Spawns, rebinding, healing and other players' damage never flash.
- [PlayerFlashlight](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Player/PlayerFlashlight.cs) on NetworkPlayer: the `Player/Flashlight` Button (F) toggles it; it starts on for every new spawn (not persisted across travel) and ignores F while controls are locked or the Steam overlay is active. On/off and camera pitch are owner-written ClientToServer SyncVars. The owner sees the shadowed **Flashlight** spot under PlayerCamera; other players see the unshadowed **RemoteFlashlight** under WorldView (originally weaker; intensities are user-tuned) aimed by the synced pitch. Tune intensity/range/angles/color on those Light components. A generated cookie gives a bright hotspot, dimmer middle and brighter rim (Hotspot/Rim settings on the component). While an EnemyFearSource renderer is inside the beam cone, in range and in line of sight, the light flickers with hard drop-outs on every client that evaluates it. 3D spot lights may not light Sprite-Lit-Default sprites.
- [PlayMode tests](../Assets/Tests/PlayMode/PlayerHudTests.cs) cover all health values, stamina fill/blink, owner-only binding, clamping, generated SyncVar serialization, persistence, duplicate prevention, respawn and reconnect. [EditMode tests](../Assets/Tests/EditMode/PlayerHudSceneTests.cs) check scene/prefab wiring. These use an in-memory Mirror host, not live Steam.

## Character sprites

- [CharacterDefinition](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Player/CharacterDefinition.cs) stores Idle, Walk, Run, Attack, and Dead with per-state **Assignment Mode** and **Frames Per Second**. Create assets with **Create > Capstone > Character Definition**. [PlayerCharacter.asset](../Assets/SPRITES/PlayerCharacter.asset) is assigned to the player prefab but needs generated or manually assigned sprite frames.
- **Automatic** is the default and preserves existing definitions. Assign a dedicated PNG per state, set its grid cell size, Pixels Per Unit, and FPS, then click **Slice [State] Sheet & Assign Frames**. [The importer](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Player/Editor/CharacterSheetImporter.cs) reads every grid cell left-to-right, top-to-bottom and splits the sequence equally in **West, South, East, North** order. Sixteen cells produce four frames per direction. Directional counts must be multiples of four; Dead uses all cells without directions. Sheet dimensions must divide exactly by the cell size; transparent cells count.
- **Manual** provides an editable **Frames Per Direction**, shared by West/South/East/North for that state, and individual Sprite slots. Dead instead has one **Frame Count**. In the PNG Inspector, set Texture Type to Sprite (2D and UI), Sprite Mode to Multiple, Apply, then slice and Apply in Unity's Sprite Editor. Drag the sprite sub-assets into the definition's slots in playback order. The optional sheet provides an **Open Sprite Editor for Manual Slicing** shortcut; manual playback does not require a sheet or generated-grid settings. All frame slots and a positive FPS are required.
- Switching to Manual retains existing frames. Changing the count preserves the leading frames of each direction separately; shrinking drops trailing frames and growing adds empty slots. Switching back to Automatic requires regeneration and overwrites manual assignments. Automatic slicing modifies shared PNG settings, so do not share sheets with incompatible grids/PPU. Automatic frames must be regenerated after changing the sheet/grid/PPU; FPS changes never require regeneration.
- `WorldView` is the visibility root controlled by [PlayerPresentation](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Player/PlayerPresentation.cs); its child `WorldSprites` carries the SpriteRenderer. [PlayerVision](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Player/PlayerVision.cs) on the player root holds both the CharacterDefinition and WorldSprites references and writes the selected frame to `SpriteRenderer.sprite`. Neither WorldView nor WorldSprites needs its own CharacterDefinition component.
- [PlayerVision](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Player/PlayerVision.cs) sends the owner's camera yaw and animation state through Mirror. Each client chooses remote artwork relative to its own player's camera yaw: same facing = North/back, opposite = South/front, observed facing toward viewer's right = East, left = West. Pitch is ignored.
- Only the child WorldSprites transform billboards locally toward the observing camera, upright and without changing the networked player root. Do not network billboard rotations or use a remote player's inactive camera as the observer.
- Idle/Walk follow actual horizontal movement automatically. Future owner gameplay can call `SetAnimationState(Run/Attack/Dead)` and `ResumeMovementAnimation()`. Idle/Walk/Run loop; Attack/Dead hold their last frame. Explicitly setting a state restarts its animation. Run speed, combat, and death controls remain deferred.
- [EditMode character tests](../Assets/Tests/EditMode/CharacterDefinitionTests.cs) verify real PNG slicing, stable generated sprite references, FPS playback, dead sequences, and viewer-relative direction math. The PlayMode player tests also verify automatic Idle/Walk states, owner camera/state Commands, SyncVar serialization, and local-only sprite/billboard changes.

## Steam playtests and invites

- [SteamSession](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Player/SteamSession.cs) initializes Steam before the transport, pumps callbacks, and stops networking before shutting down Steam. Initialization failures disable the HUD and transport and show an error. Steam must be running with the testing account logged in.
- Use the HUD's **Host (Server + Client)** to host. Guests can enter the host's SteamID64 in the HUD and click **Client**. The scene displays the local SteamID64. FizzySteamworks uses Steam IDs, not localhost/IP addresses; test guests with separate Steam accounts.
- [PlayerInteraction](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Player/PlayerInteraction.cs) reads the owner-only Button `Player/Use` action (E). It raycasts from the local camera forward, up to 3.5 units; solid obstacles block it. Interactive objects derive from [Interactable](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Player/Interactable.cs) (`Prompt`, `CanInteract`, `Interact`); objects whose `CanInteract` is false are not targeted. [SteamInviteInteractable](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Player/SteamInviteInteractable.cs) can be attached to an object with a non-trigger collider (including a child collider). A placeholder SteamInviteTerminal is already in SampleScene.
- Nametags: the HUD's bottom-centre **Nametag** ([NametagHud](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Player/NametagHud.cs) on the PlayerHud prefab: exposed **Font** applied to NameText/PromptText, Show Prompt, **Prompt Format** "[E] {0}") shows what the local camera's centre aims at (`PlayerInteraction.AimedName`, **Nametag Distance** 12). Objects get a name by adding [Nametag](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Player/Nametag.cs) (**Display Name**, **Max Distance** 3.5) next to their collider; SampleScene's invite terminal, jeepney and map terminal have one. Interactables additionally show their `Prompt` within 3.5 units (this replaced the old OnGUI prompt box). Living other players show their [PlayerName](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Player/PlayerName.cs) (on NetworkPlayer: SyncVar set by the owner's Command from `SteamFriends.GetPersonaName()`, sanitized, max 32 characters, fallback "Player {netId}"). Remote CharacterControllers are disabled, so players are aimed with a ray-vs-capsule test of each controller's shape (`PlayerName.TryAimDistance`); nearer solid colliders still hide them. Live Steam names need separate-account testing.
- [PlayerControlLock](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Player/PlayerControlLock.cs) is a static owner set: while any owner holds it (menus, travel), movement/gravity, look and interaction pause and the cursor is released. Always `Release` the same owner (e.g. in OnDisable/OnDestroy).
- Hosting creates a friends-only Steam matchmaking lobby for invitations/discovery only; the lobby remains the playable SampleScene, not a waiting-room scene. [SteamNetworkManager](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Player/SteamNetworkManager.cs) shares the lobby ID over a Mirror NetworkMessage with all clients, including manually connected guests. E opens `ActivateGameOverlayInviteDialog(lobbyId)` for actual play invitations. The lobby stores a project marker (Spacewar is shared by unrelated games) and the host SteamID64. Accepting `GameLobbyJoinRequested_t` enters the lobby, validates its metadata/owner, and starts the FizzySteamworks client automatically.
- SteamSession publishes the `connect` rich-presence key for Join Game and still handles `GameRichPresenceJoinRequested_t`, launch `+connect`, and launch `+connect_lobby`. Disconnect before accepting an invite when already hosting/connected. Leaving clears presence and lobby membership; the host closes the lobby and removes its address. Host migration is not supported. Lobby/API errors are logged; E can be retried after asynchronous lobby creation/entry completes.
- Enable Steam Overlay and test invitation UI in a standalone build; it may be unavailable in the Unity Editor. Put the temporary `steam_appid.txt` (480) beside the executable for local development builds. Replace the App ID for release. Movement and interaction pause while Steam Overlay is active.
- With Spacewar's App ID, both testers should already have this project's build running before accepting an invite. Steam cannot reliably cold-launch this custom executable through Spacewar's app configuration; cold-launch invitations need the project's own Steam app configured for distribution.
- [Steam scene tests](../Assets/Tests/EditMode/SteamSceneTests.cs) check scene/prefab/input wiring and invite-address validation. PlayMode tests cover spawn registration and owner-only, range-limited, obstruction-aware E interaction. These do not prove live Steam connectivity or overlay behavior; verify those using separate Steam accounts.

## Local camera and endless-night atmosphere

- The player prefab's Camera has a **Far Clip Plane** (40 units originally; user-tuned) and post-processing/depth enabled. Adjust Far Clip Plane on the prefab; no script overwrites it. On NetworkPlayer > PlayerCamera, [PlayerCameraEffects](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Player/PlayerCameraEffects.cs) exposes **World pixelation** with a Pixelation toggle and **Pixel Height** (270 originally; user-tuned). Lower values (e.g. 135) make larger pixels; higher values (e.g. 540) make finer pixels, capped at the camera's output resolution. Changes apply immediately; the horizontal resolution follows the camera's aspect ratio. This quantizes the world image, not mesh geometry, and leaves Screen Space Overlay UI crisp.
- [NightVisionRendererFeature](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Player/NightVisionRendererFeature.cs) is installed on both PC and Mobile URP renderer assets. It uses Unity 6 RenderGraph and requires an intermediate color texture. Only enabled Game cameras carrying PlayerCameraEffects receive the custom passes; remote cameras remain inactive through PlayerPresentation. Fog runs before post-processing; pixelation runs after it. Keep first-person HUD/sprites on Screen Space Overlay canvases so UI remains crisp.
- The scene's existing Global Volume uses [SampleSceneProfile](../Assets/Settings/SampleSceneProfile.asset). **Film Grain > Intensity** controls noise strength (0 disables it; originally 0.35, user-tuned), with Response available for brightness sensitivity. The look is dark and neutral rather than blue: Color Adjustments use Post Exposure -0.7 (was -1.1; lightened on request), a neutral color filter and -35 saturation. NightFog's Ambient Color is (0.003, 0.003, 0.0035) and Density 0.05. Scene ambient is (0.008, 0.008, 0.009) in SampleScene and (0.004, 0.004, 0.0045) in StreetsTest. Both scenes use Custom environment reflections with no cubemap and Reflection Intensity 0: unbaked default skybox reflections tint every lit surface grey and wash out the darkness. The player camera's background is black. SampleScene keeps a neutral shadowed directional moon light (intensity 0.08) because NightFog's light shafts depend on it. Scene Lighting has no daylight skybox. Player flashlights provide most visibility.
- **Enemy Pixel Detail** on PlayerCameraEffects (2 by default) makes renderers marked with [ReducedPixelation](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Player/ReducedPixelation.cs) use a finer pixel grid than the world (1 = same as the world). A mask pass draws those renderers depth-tested against the scene, so walls in front still use the world grid. The Tikbalang's WorldSprites carries the marker; add it to future enemy sprite renderers.
- **Capstone > Night Fog** in that profile is a true depth-terminated ray march, not Unity's distance-fog switch. [NightFog](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Player/NightFog.cs) exposes Enabled, Density, Max Distance, Base Height, Height Falloff, Ambient Color, Light Scattering, Anisotropy, and Steps. More steps reduce banding but increase GPU cost. Fog distance is capped by Camera.farClipPlane. Main directional-light shadows produce shafts (**Light Scattering**); up to eight visible point/spot lights contribute unshadowed scattering with their own **Local Light Scattering** (0.2) that fades in over **Local Light Near Fade** (3 m) from the lamp, so a flashlight shows a faint beam instead of a glowing blob at the lens and its light reads on the surfaces it hits (local-light shadows/cookies are not simulated). URP lights fall off with inverse square, so the owner Flashlight uses intensity 8 and range 30 to reach buildings. Transparent materials without depth writes use the opaque depth behind them.
- Night sky: [NightSky.mat](../Assets/Settings/NightSky.mat) ([Capstone/Night Sky](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Player/NightSky.shader), moon math shared with the fog via [NightSkyMoon.hlsl](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Player/NightSkyMoon.hlsl)) is the skybox of SampleScene and StreetsTest; the player camera clears to Skybox. It draws a Zenith/Horizon gradient, **Below Horizon Color** and a **Moon Sprite** (alpha; Azimuth 0 = +Z, 90 = +X, Elevation, Size in degrees, optional glow) only where no geometry is. There is no horizon strip. Night Fog covers the whole sky exactly like geometry at Max Distance; only the moon (and its glow) shows through, dimmed by NightFog's **Moon Fog** (0.35; 0 = undimmed, 1 = fogged like the sky). Ambient stays Flat, so the skybox never lights the scene. Post Exposure/grain/pixelation still apply; brighten the moon with the HDR tint. Blood moon: [MoonSky](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Player/MoonSky.cs) on each scene's Directional Light swaps between **Normal Sky** (NightSky) and **Blood Moon Sky** ([BloodMoonSky.mat](../Assets/Settings/BloodMoonSky.mat): same moon, red tint/glow/gradient) and sets the light to **Blood Moon Light Color** x **Intensity Multiplier** (1.5), so fog light shafts turn red; it restores the light's own color/intensity otherwise. The static `MoonSky.BloodMoon` persists across scenes and is applied immediately by every MoonSky (context menu toggles it in Play Mode). It is local state: future difficulty code must set it on every peer (e.g. with the travel/difficulty message). Add MoonSky to every new map scene's moon light. Moon alignment: MoonSky's **Align Moon To Light** (default on, also in Edit Mode) publishes `-light.forward` as the global `_NightSkyMoonLight`, overriding the material Azimuth/Elevation for both the skybox and fog moon, so the moonlight comes from the visible moon; rotate the Directional Light to move the moon (both scenes use rotation (22, 215, 0), matching the old azimuth 35/elevation 22). The moon is excluded from world pixelation: the pixel pass blends full-resolution pixels back in wherever the sky's moon sprite mask is set.
- Leave built-in scene Fog disabled to avoid double fog. Pixelation does not lower the cost of rendering geometry; ray marching adds work, so profile on target hardware. [NightVisionTests](../Assets/Tests/EditMode/NightVisionTests.cs) check asset wiring; [NightVisionRenderTests](../Assets/Tests/PlayMode/NightVisionRenderTests.cs) measure rendered pixel blocks, grain variance, fog attenuation, fogged sky with the moon showing through (Moon Fog), the blood moon swap, light scattering/shadows, and crisp overlay UI. The overlay screenshot test requires a non-batch Editor run because batch mode lacks Unity's end-of-frame screenshot stage; other render tests support batch mode.

## Local enemy-spotting panic

- Attach [EnemyFearSource](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Player/EnemyFearSource.cs) to an enemy root and assign its body Renderer (or let it find the first child Renderer). It works with mesh, skinned-mesh, or sprite renderers. Full Intensity Distance and Max Distance control linear camera-to-renderer-center falloff; Intensity scales the target's maximum effect. SampleScene contains no fear test object anymore (the EnemyFearTest cube was removed); the Tikbalang prefab carries an EnemyFearSource.
- [PlayerFearEffects](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Player/PlayerFearEffects.cs) is on the prefab's PlayerCamera. Only the local owner's enabled camera evaluates sources; no panic state is networked and no shared Volume is modified. Visible renderer bounds are sampled at their center and six face centers, inside the camera's frustum/clipping range, with solid-collider line-of-sight checks. This is a sampled visibility approximation, not GPU pixel/occlusion readback. Walls need colliders on the Occlusion Mask; triggers and the owner's/target's colliders are ignored. Use the strongest visible source, not additive stacking.
- Proximity: EnemyFearSource's **Proximity Full Distance** (2) / **Proximity Max Distance** (10; 0 disables) drive `ProximityIntensity` regardless of sight or walls. The vignette and vertical lines follow `OverlayIntensity` (the stronger of sight and proximity, smoothed); the FOV shudder stays sight-only (`CurrentIntensity`). Chase state itself is not yet a fear input; `TikbalangBrain.ChaseTarget` is synced for that later.
- Camera controls expose Build Up/Recovery Speed, extra Vignette Strength, Vertical Grain Strength/Line Count/Line Thickness/Film Jitter Speed, and FOV Shudder/Frequency. **Vertical Line Thickness** is a relative width multiplier: 1 restores the original width, 0.5 (the default) halves it, and smaller values make finer scratches without changing line count or panic intensity. Extremely thin scratches may fall below screen resolution. The shader layers dark edges and continuous, full-height vertical film scratches over the default post-processing, after world pixel sampling and before overlay UI. Film Jitter Speed changes the lines between film frames without introducing vertical gaps within a frame. FOV shudder is bounded around the configured FOV and restores on recovery, camera/view disable, or despawn. Set FOV Shudder to zero to disable camera motion.
- [PlayerFearEffectsTests](../Assets/Tests/PlayMode/PlayerFearEffectsTests.cs) cover distance, sight, occlusion, partial visibility, independent cameras, source lifecycle and FOV restoration. NetworkPlayerTests check ownership even when a remote camera is forcibly enabled; NightVisionRenderTests measure edge darkening, vertical scratch structure and unchanged shared grain.

## Street block generator (PCG map blocks)

- Goal: REPO-style procedural streets built from pre-generated outdoor "blocks" connected at their entrances. Blocks are authored with this tool and connected at runtime by MapManager (see Scene travel and MapManager). Level code lives in [Assets/SCRIPTS/Level](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Level) (`Capstone.Level` asmdef; editor code in `Capstone.Level.Editor`).
- Author blocks in [StreetBlockWorkshop](../Assets/Scenes/StreetBlockWorkshop.unity) or via **GameObject > Capstone > Street Block Generator**. [StreetBlockGenerator](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Level/StreetBlockGenerator.cs) holds the settings; its inspector offers **Generate**, **New Seed & Generate**, **Clear Generated**, and **Save As Prefab** (to `Prefab Folder`/`Prefab Name`, default `Assets/PREFABS/StreetBlocks`). Saved prefabs are plain copies; keep the workshop object unpacked so it stays regenerable. Generation is deterministic per seed and rebuilds the `Generated/{Floor, Obstacles, Buildings, Walls, Boundaries, Decorations}` children; failed generation keeps the previous result.
- Size is `Size In Tiles` of the floor prefab (default [Path_Road](../Assets/Prefab/Streets%20Object/Path_Road.prefab), 3 x 3 m). Tiles group into grid cells of `Tiles Per Cell`; the size must be a multiple of it. All blocks that connect must use the same cell size. Block origin is the floor center with Y=0 at the floor top.
- Entrances (0-4): Random or Manual sides (West/South/East/North), centered or random cell, at least 2 tiles wide and at most one cell. A clear L-shaped walkway runs from every entrance to the block center; buildings, walls and decorations never overlap it. [StreetBlock](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Level/StreetBlock.cs) stores entrances (side, cell, width, local center, obstacle) and draws gizmos (green open, red obstructed).
- Buildings are placed along the perimeter facing inward (prefab front = +Z). Everything, including roofs/overhangs measured from renderer and collider bounds, must stay inside the floor; an oversized building/wall/obstacle/decoration aborts generation with an error naming its size and the floor size. Walls follow **Wall Mode**: *Fill Gaps* (default) puts buildings on the edge and fills only the closed-edge gaps they leave; *Wrap Edges* first wraps the whole edge (except entrances) with wall pieces and then sets each side's buildings back behind its deepest wall piece, without overlapping walls. In both modes each closed span runs corner to corner (corner wall pieces may overlap each other, never buildings) and ends with a closing piece placed flush against the span end, so walls meet entrances and their gates/obstacles without gaps. Only spans no wall piece fits get invisible `Boundary Height` box colliders. Saved block prefabs keep their old output until regenerated: select them and use **Assets > Capstone > Regenerate Selected Street Block Prefabs** (re-runs generation with each prefab's saved seed/settings, replacing manual edits under `Generated`). **Middle Buildings** (Count 0 = edges only, keeping old seeds' layouts) are placed after the edges are sealed, inside the block: **Middle Building Prefabs** (empty = Building Prefabs), **Middle Building Clearance** (1.5 m walkable gap to the floor edge, walls, edge buildings and each other; they may touch but never cover a walkway) and **Middle Building Facing** (Toward Walkway = front turns to the nearest entrance walkway, or Random 90-degree yaw). Ones that cannot fit are skipped with a warning. **Filler mode** (Entrance Count 0, or Manual with no sides ticked; the inspector shows a note) packs the interior instead: **Filler Building Prefabs** (empty = Middle, then Building Prefabs) are placed row by row in all four turns, favouring larger footprints with random variety, leaving only **Filler Alley Width** (1.2 m) alleys to the edge and between buildings; Middle Building Count is ignored, and **Filler Edge Buildings Face Outward** (on) turns perimeter buildings' fronts to the neighbouring streets. Decorations scatter with spacing; ones that cannot fit are skipped with a warning. Project prefabs had no colliders, so `Add Missing Colliders` adds box colliders (plus a floor collider).
- Obstacles: put closed/breakable prefabs carrying [EntranceObstacle](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Level/EntranceObstacle.cs) in the generator's **Obstacle Prefabs** list. `Obstacle Count` entrances receive a random entry. Requirement is Key, Destruction or KeyAndDestruction; gameplay calls `TryUseKey`/`TryDestroy` **on the server** (offline also works); key/axe inventory is still deferred. Optional **Cleared Prefab** overrides deactivation: closed renderers, colliders and carvers turn off and the opened/broken prefab appears as a child at local position/rotation zero and scale one. Match its origin/orientation/scale to the closed prefab; author any remaining solid colliders on the opened prefab, not across the passage. It must not contain EntranceObstacle or NetworkIdentity. Without it, **Deactivate When Cleared** keeps its existing behavior, but closed colliders/carvers always turn off. `cleared` fires once on each peer. Gate 1/2 Closed (Key) and Breakable (Destruction) reference their matching opened prefabs (`Gate X (Opened)` and `Gate X Open` respectively); opened variants are visuals, not obstacle pool entries.
- [EntranceObstacleNetwork](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Level/EntranceObstacleNetwork.cs), registered by SteamNetworkManager, broadcasts server changes and supplies late-join snapshots including inactive and partially fulfilled obstacles. Obstacles remain local map objects, not Mirror spawn prefabs. Their scene hierarchy and generated map seed must match on every peer; map completion and scene arrival request snapshots to recover changes received during loading. [EntranceObstacleNetworkTests](../Assets/Tests/PlayMode/EntranceObstacleNetworkTests.cs) cover in-memory message delivery, snapshots, replica application and the client authority guard; live Steam behavior still requires separate-account playtests. Small blocks with several wide entrances leave little room for buildings/decorations.
- [StreetBlockGeneratorTests](../Assets/Tests/EditMode/StreetBlockGeneratorTests.cs) check footprint containment, colliders, clear entrances, raycast-sealed edges, corner coverage and flush entrance walls in both wall modes, filler packing/alleys, determinism, oversized-roof errors, manual sides/obstacles, obstacle requirements, and the real project assets/workshop.

## Scene travel and MapManager

- Players persist across scene changes: [PlayerPersistence](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Player/PlayerPersistence.cs) on NetworkPlayer marks it DontDestroyOnLoad. The host's player object survives as-is; Mirror hides and respawns each guest's own player from the server's copy of that player, so every player keeps their own state (never the host's). Health is server-authoritative. Stamina is owner-simulated, so at travel begin each owner sends its exact stamina/exhaustion/regen delay via `PlayerStamina.CommitForTravel()`, and `PlayerStamina.TravelPaused` freezes regeneration and stamina use on every client until the fade-in; respawned guests restore the delay in `OnStartAuthority`. [SteamNetworkManager](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Player/SteamNetworkManager.cs) re-readies existing players after scene changes instead of adding new ones. Add future per-player state (e.g. inventory) as server-held SyncVars/SyncLists on the player prefab; owner-simulated state needs a similar travel handoff.
- [TravelDirector](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Player/TravelDirector.cs) sits on the persistent NetworkManager object (Loading Screen Prefab, Fade Duration, Loading Reveal Duration, Ready Timeout, Minimum Loading Seconds = 8). Any player may choose a destination and start travel; the server validates requests (only at base, listed on a MapTerminal in the active scene, not the current scene, in the Build Profile). Host migration is not supported.
- [MapTerminal](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Player/MapTerminal.cs) (E) works only at base (`MapTerminal.TravelMapAvailable`: RoundClock's base scene, or no enabled RoundClock); away from base the jeepney back is the only way home. It has an editable **Destinations** list ([TravelDestination](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Player/TravelDestination.cs): Scene Name plus a weighted **Enemy Pool** of [EnemyDefinition](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Enemies/EnemyDefinition.cs) assets, **Create > Capstone > Enemy Definition**, e.g. [Tikbalang](../Assets/PREFABS/Enemies/Definitions/Tikbalang.asset)) and opens the persistent [TravelMapScreen](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Player/TravelMapScreen.cs) ([prefab](../Assets/PREFABS/TravelMapScreen.prefab): map background, destination buttons, confirmation). The current scene and scenes not in the Build Profile are grayed out and disabled. Yes closes the panels and selects the destination for everyone; No/Escape close the confirmation, then the map. Every map button has [HoverRevealGraphic](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Player/HoverRevealGraphic.cs): its background (Target, default the Button's Target Graphic) stays fully transparent, still clickable, until hovered, then fades (**Fade Seconds**) to **Hover Alpha**; disabled buttons stay hidden unless Reveal When Not Interactable. Add it to future UI buttons.
- UI font: new UI texts use blood_crow ([bloodcrow.ttf](../Assets/Fonts/blood_crow/bloodcrow.ttf)), like the travel map, loading screen and nametag.
- Enemy roll: the server rolls one enemy type per destination (weighted; an empty pool rolls none) when a scene's terminals become active and shares it with all clients (`TravelEnemyRollMessage`). The confirmation shows "Enemies: [Name]", "None", or "Unknown" before the roll arrives. Starting travel clears the terminal rolls; the arrival scene keeps the roll chosen before the trip (`TravelDirector.ArrivalEnemy`), and its EnemySpawner spawns that enemy instead of its own entries. The new scene's terminals roll again. Scenes opened directly without travel use the spawner's own list. The confirmation also shows the travel time (see Round clock). Difficulty and gas stats are deferred.
- [TravelInteractable](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Player/TravelInteractable.cs) (the jeepney back) is pre-placed and only targetable once a destination is selected. Travel: everyone locks controls and fades to black, the host calls `ServerChangeScene`, the [loading screen](../Assets/PREFABS/TravelLoadingScreen.prefab) shows (black Background, centred "Loading" text whose dots animate per Loading Message/Max Dots/Dot Interval on [TravelLoadingScreen](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Player/TravelLoadingScreen.cs), a random tip/lore TipText below it, and a bottom EnemyRow), every client builds the map and reports ready (or Ready Timeout passes), the server also waits until the screen has been visible for Minimum Loading Seconds (ServerTravel trips only, including returns to base; late joiners are not delayed), players are moved to the scene's spawn points, then the screen fades black, the loading screen hides, and the game fades in.
- Loading tips/lore live in [LoadingTips.asset](../Assets/Settings/LoadingTips.asset) ([LoadingTips](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Player/LoadingTips.cs), **Create > Capstone > Loading Tips**): add a line to its **Tips** list ("TIP: " prefix for gameplay tips). Each loading screen shows one at random (never the same twice in a row); **Tip Change Interval** on TravelLoadingScreen (0 = one per screen) rotates them.
- [MapManager](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Level/MapManager.cs) is scene-local (one per map scene) with **Connector Blocks** (2+ entrances), **End Cap Blocks** (1 entrance) and **Spawn Blocks** (1 entrance) pools and **Connector Block Count** (end caps and the spawn block are extra). [MapLayoutPlanner](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Level/MapLayoutPlanner.cs) grows blocks with 90-degree rotations, matches opposite sides of equal width, rejects footprint overlaps, closes every remaining entrance with an end cap, and puts the spawn block at the far edge. **Loop Chance** (0.75; 0 = tree only, keeping old seeds' layouts) is the per-step chance to place a connector that joins two or more open entrances at once, closing a loop; loops need multi-entrance connectors (e.g. crossroads) in the pool. After layout, MapManager records every connected entrance pair as a `MapJoint` (`Joints`, `LoopCount`) and keeps at most one obstacle per joint. Joints with no baked obstacle roll **End Cap Obstacle Chance** (1) or **Loop Obstacle Chance** (0.35) and MapManager places one itself (own seeded random, so all peers match): a random prefab from the host block's generator **Obstacle Prefabs** (end caps host their own gate; else the other block's list, else **Fallback Obstacle Prefabs**), under the host's `Generated/Obstacles`, outer face on the block edge, centred and facing inward, assigned to that entrance. Generator **Obstacle Count** can therefore stay 0. The same keep rules below apply. End-cap joints keep a barricade (**Barricade End Caps**): these are the only fully sealed places, intended for loot behind the obstacle later. Connector-to-connector barricades are kept (**Barricade Loops**) only if every non-end-cap block stays reachable from spawn without crossing a barricade, so they sit on loops and players can always walk around them. The spawn block's entrance obstacles and any obstacle within its opening (half width + 1 m) are also removed, so the spawn entrance is never blocked. `IsJointOpen`, `FindOpenlyReachable(block)` and `FindOpenlyReachableFromSpawn()` report which blocks can be walked to without crossing an uncleared barricade (updates live as gates are opened). All blocks need the same cell size. Generation is deterministic from a seed: the host sends it with travel and every peer builds locally (map blocks are not networked objects). Offline it uses Fixed Seed or a random one; use the component's context menu to preview/clear in the Editor without saving preview blocks.
- Spawn points: with **Generate Spawn Points** on, the placed spawn block gets a "PlayerSpawnPoints (Generated)" child with up to **Spawn Point Count** (6) points, at least **Spawn Point Spacing** (1.5 m) apart, nearest the block centre and facing the entrance. Candidates (0.5 m grid) need block floor underneath, a free player capsule (**Spawn Clearance Radius** 0.45, **Height** 2) against the block's generated solids, and a walkable path from the entrance. Spawn blocks that already contain a PlayerSpawnPoints with children keep theirs.
- Filler blocks: **Filler Blocks** (0 entrances, same cell size; make them with Entrance Count 0) fill every free cell of the street's bounding box plus **Filler Margin Cells** (2), largest first with random rotations, under a "Fillers" child. They use their own seeded random, so street layouts are unchanged, and are excluded from Layout, BlockCount, neighbours and the NavMesh. Fillers may overhang the outer margin so large fillers reach it. Cells no filler fits (e.g. 1-2 cell gaps between street blocks) are plugged when **Plug Gaps** is on (default): the smallest filler's floor tiles plus one **Gap Fill Prefab** centred per cell with a random quarter turn (empty list = that filler's generator Filler/Middle/Building Prefabs; prefabs larger than a cell are skipped), under Fillers/Gap Plugs (`PluggedCellCount`).
- Navigation (play mode only, every peer): after building, MapManager bakes one runtime NavMesh (AI Navigation's core `UnityEngine.AI` NavMeshBuilder, **Nav Mesh Agent Type Id** 0 = Humanoid) from each block's floor colliders (`StreetBlock.FloorRoot`, default `Generated/Floor`), then gives every other solid collider (buildings, walls, decorations, entrance obstacles) a child carving box NavMeshObstacle when **Carve Obstacles** is on. Carving pads every box by the baked agent radius: **Bake Agent Radius** (0.3; 0 = the agent type's 0.5) sets that padding and wall clearance for the bake. **Decoration Carve Scale** (0.6) shrinks decoration carvers horizontally, because generator-added colliders use full renderer bounds (e.g. tree canopies). A [NavMeshCarveOverride](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Level/NavMeshCarveOverride.cs) on any prefab replaces its carving with one Custom footprint box (center/size/height, gizmo when selected) or None. [StreetNavMeshTests](../Assets/Tests/PlayMode/StreetNavMeshTests.cs) cover this. `EntranceObstacle` disables its child NavMeshObstacles when cleared so the NavMesh fills in. `Built` fires after the bake. MapManager also exposes `BlockCount`, `GetBlock`, `GetRole`, `GetNeighbours` (edge-touching blocks) and `TryGetBlockIndex(position)` for AI.
- Placeholders: [StreetsTest](../Assets/Scenes/StreetsTest.unity) (in the Build Profile, no NetworkManager) uses the user's blocks in [StreetBlocks](../Assets/PREFABS/StreetBlocks) (StreetBlock_2Entrances_N, StreetBlock_3Entrances_N, IntersectStreetBlock_N, EndBlockStreetBlock_N, SpawnBlockStreetBlock_N; 6 m cells). The spawn blocks get generated spawn points but currently contain no jeepney TravelInteractable back to SampleScene; add one to them. No MapTerminal. SampleScene has a MapTerminal and a jeepney TravelInteractable; their positions are approximate. Map scenes must not contain their own NetworkManager.
- The travel begin message carries the destination's rolled enemy asset ids; each client finds that prefab's [EnemyLoadingMiniature](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Player/EnemyLoadingMiniature.cs) (Frames, Frames Per Second, Display Height in 1920x1080 reference pixels) via NetworkClient.prefabs, so enemy prefabs must be in the NetworkManager's Spawn Prefabs. Distinct miniatures are cloned from the inactive MiniatureTemplate UI Image into EnemyRow's HorizontalLayoutGroup (UI Images, not SpriteRenderers, because layout groups only arrange RectTransforms); the row hides when no enemies were rolled. Add an EnemyLoadingMiniature to every new enemy prefab; Tikbalang uses TikbalangLoading-Sheet's 8 frames.
- [MapTravelTests](../Assets/Tests/EditMode/MapTravelTests.cs) check rotation math, connected/non-overlapping layouts across seeds, spawn placement, generated unobstructed spawn points, map-placed joint obstacles, filler coverage and gap plugs, determinism, pool errors and asset/scene wiring. [TravelTests](../Assets/Tests/PlayMode/TravelTests.cs) cover the control lock, map screen, loading screen (dots, enemy row layout/animation) and an in-memory host trip (minimum loading time, rolled Tikbalang miniature) to StreetsTest (persistent player/health/exact stamina, built map, spawn arrival, fade-in); NetworkPlayerTests cover the stamina travel pause, the owner's Command and a simulated guest respawn keeping its own stamina. Live Steam multi-client travel must be verified with separate Steam accounts.

## Enemies and the Tikbalang

- Enemy code lives in [Assets/SCRIPTS/Enemies](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Enemies) (`Capstone.Enemies` asmdef, referencing Mirror, Capstone.Level and Capstone.Player; editor code in `Capstone.Enemies.Editor`). Enemies are server-authoritative: the prefab's NavMeshAgent is disabled and only the server enables it (`EnemyMotor.Activate`) once a NavMesh exists; NetworkTransformReliable syncs the root. Brains move through the abstract [EnemyLocomotion](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Enemies/EnemyLocomotion.cs) (`EnemyBrain.Locomotion`): [EnemyMotor](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Enemies/EnemyMotor.cs) for NavMesh walkers (`EnemyBrain.Motor`, null for flyers) or [EnemyFlightMotor](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Enemies/EnemyFlightMotor.cs) for flyers. Networked enemy prefabs must be in SampleScene's NetworkManager **Registered Spawnable Prefabs**. While `TravelDirector.ServerLoadingActive` (fading out, loading, and 2x Fade Duration after arrival for the fade-in) `EnemyBrain.IsFrozenForLoading` is true and every brain stops its locomotion and skips its states, so enemies neither move nor attack behind the loading screen; TravelTests check this.
- FSM: [EnemyBrain](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Enemies/EnemyBrain.cs) is the main brain (server-only Update, synced `StateName`, home area, hidden-teleport helpers); each state is its own [EnemyState](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Enemies/EnemyState.cs) script. [TikbalangBrain](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Enemies/Tikbalang/TikbalangBrain.cs) has Idle, Searching, Chase, Returning and Stunned states. Tuning lives in a [TikbalangProfile](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Enemies/Tikbalang/TikbalangProfile.cs) asset ([Tikbalang_Default](../Assets/PREFABS/Enemies/Profiles/Tikbalang_Default.asset)); a harder variant should be another profile asset.
- Movement must be snappy for all enemies: [EnemyMotor](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Enemies/EnemyMotor.cs) uses instant acceleration/stops/turns (no agent rotation), and [EnemyPresentation](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Enemies/EnemyPresentation.cs) steps the visible sprite position at **Snaps Per Second** (12; jumps over 5 m show immediately). The body may keep facing a target (`LookTarget`) while the sprite direction always follows actual movement.
- Sprites: [EnemySpriteDefinition](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Enemies/EnemySpriteDefinition.cs) (**Create > Capstone > Enemy Sprite Definition**) has directional Idle and Moving animations with the same Automatic/Manual slicing inspector as CharacterDefinition. Direction/billboarding use the player rules (relative to the local player's camera; only the WorldSprites child billboards). Until frames are assigned a dark placeholder silhouette (**Placeholder Size**) shows. [Tikbalang_Sprites](../Assets/SPRITES/Enemies/Tikbalang_Sprites.asset) has user-assigned frames (WorldSprites scale 0.5).
- Solid sprites: depth-based effects (Night Fog, reduced pixelation) read the depth texture, so transparent sprites without depth writes (e.g. Sprite-Unlit-Default) get the fog and light scattering of the scene *behind* them and look see-through. Enemy WorldSprites use [SolidSprite.mat](../Assets/PREFABS/Materials/SolidSprite.mat) ([Capstone/Solid Sprite](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Player/SolidSprite.shader): unlit, alpha cutout at **Alpha Cutoff** 0.5, AlphaTest queue, ZWrite plus DepthOnly/DepthNormalsOnly passes). Use it for future enemy sprites; player WorldSprites still use Sprite-Unlit-Default. The shader reads SpriteRenderer.color through URP's `unity_SpriteColor` (tint and flip work); texture alpha is cut out, while the color's alpha is alpha-blended (no dither, so pixelation stays even).
- Distance fade: [DistanceFadeSprite](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Player/DistanceFadeSprite.cs) (local only: each peer uses its own local player's camera, else Camera.main, and changes only its own renderers) sets its **Renderers** (empty = all child SpriteRenderers) by camera distance. Opacity: solid up to **Solid Distance** (12 m), eased to **Minimum Opacity** (0.01 originally; user-tuned) at **Faded Distance** (30 m originally; user-tuned). Darkening: full colour up to **Darken Start Distance** (4 m), eased to **Minimum Brightness** (0.15, sRGB multiplier) at **Darkest Distance** (25 m). It multiplies each renderer's original color and restores color/material when disabled. While faded, Solid Sprite renderers switch to a cached local transparent copy of their material (`_ZWrite` 0, Transparent queue, DepthOnly/DepthNormalsOnly off), so faded sprites are fogged with the scene behind them; at full opacity they return to the depth-writing material. The Tikbalang root has it (WorldSprites); add it to every new enemy/item with billboarded sprites.
- Ground shadow: a **BlobShadow** child (built-in Quad, [BlobShadow.mat](../Assets/PREFABS/Materials/BlobShadow.mat) with [Capstone/Blob Shadow](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Player/BlobShadow.shader), no collider) runs [BlobShadow](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Player/BlobShadow.cs) locally on every peer after presentation: it follows the snapped WorldSprites horizontally, raycasts down (**Max Ground Distance** 5, ignoring triggers and the enemy's own colliders), lies flat on the hit surface and hides when no ground is found. Tune **Diameter** (1.3 m) and **Opacity** (0.7) on the component and Edge Softness on the material.
- Senses ([EnemySenses](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Enemies/EnemySenses.cs), server): vision is a cone (full **Vision Angle**, default 40 degrees, 18 m, eyes at 2.2 m) blocked by solid colliders on the Occlusion Mask; hearing is a dome (8 m). [NoiseSystem](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Player/NoiseSystem.cs) holds noise sources and timed pulses (`EmitPulse`); a noise is heard when its dome intersects the hearing dome. [PlayerNoise](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Player/PlayerNoise.cs) on NetworkPlayer emits a 6 m dome while sprinting (owner-reported SyncVar, like stamina). Future noise makers implement `INoiseSource` or call `EmitPulse` on the server.
- Tikbalang behaviour: Idle guards its home block, walking (2.5 m/s) to random NavMesh points and standing 10 s at each. A noise inside the home block starts Searching (cone widens to 80 degrees, walks to the origin, looks around in snapped turns, then Idle; 20 s timeout); noises outside home are ignored. Seeing a player inside the home block (Idle) or any player (Searching) starts Chase: locks onto that first player anywhere at 6 m/s for 60 s, eyes on the target. Touching the target (horizontal distance within **Attack Range** 1.4 m, height difference up to 2.5 m) deals **Contact Damage** 2 (one heart) through `PlayerHealth.TakeDamage`, then the Tikbalang stands still for **Hit Pause Seconds** (1.5) before resuming; the chase ends if the target reaches 0 health. If the target is over 35 m away it teleports (5 s cooldown) to a spot hidden from every player (behind cover or beyond camera far clip, at least 10 m away) in the block next to the target's block that is closest to the target and openly reachable from it (never a sealed block). Afterwards Returning walks home ignoring players, then Idle. `Stun(seconds)` (server) drops the chase, stands still, then returns home; nothing calls it yet.
- [EnemySpawner](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Enemies/EnemySpawner.cs) (server only) waits for the scene's MapManager and NavMesh, then spawns each entry's count in random blocks that are openly reachable from spawn (never sealed behind an uncleared barricade, e.g. a gated end cap) and neither a spawn block nor adjacent to one (adjacency relaxed with a warning if none exist) and makes that block the enemy's home. StreetsTest has one with a single Tikbalang. Enemies spawned without a map guard a fallback box around their position. Brains with `RoamsWholeMap` (flyers) skip NavMesh sampling and spawn at the chosen block's centre.- Deferred: stun sources, enemy death, chase-driven fear effects and the hard variant. Enemy senses and noise ignore dead players. [EnemySetupTests](../Assets/Tests/EditMode/EnemySetupTests.cs) check prefab/profile/scene wiring; [TikbalangTests](../Assets/Tests/PlayMode/TikbalangTests.cs) cover noise overlap, the vision cone/occlusion/widening, Idle wander, Searching, sprint hearing, Chase lock/timeout/Returning, contact damage and hit pause, Stun, sprite direction vs. eyes, snappy sprite steps and hidden teleports with a runtime NavMesh and in-memory host; [BlobShadowTests](../Assets/Tests/PlayMode/BlobShadowTests.cs) cover ground placement/follow/hiding and NightVisionRenderTests check that solid sprites are fogged only by the air in front of them; TravelTests check the street NavMesh, carving obstacles and the spawner's block rules. Live Steam behaviour is unverified.

### Manananggal (flyer)

- [Manananggal.prefab](../Assets/PREFABS/Enemies/Manananggal.prefab) reuses every Tikbalang component (senses, presentation, fear source, jumpscare, loading miniature, distance fade, blob shadow, NetworkTransformReliable) but has no NavMeshAgent: [EnemyFlightMotor](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Enemies/EnemyFlightMotor.cs) flies straight when a sphere cast to the goal is clear, otherwise climbs above the highest roof ahead plus **Obstacle Clearance** and only moves horizontally once clear, so it flies over walls/buildings instead of through them (ignoring its own and players' colliders). Chasing a player under a roof/overhang (`IsCovered`: sky blocked above them), `ApproachPoint` finds an opening: it searches **Entry Search Radius** (15 m) in 16 directions for the nearest open-sky spot with a clear straight line to the player, flies there and then underneath (re-searched when the target moves 1 m or every 0.5 s). If no opening exists (fully enclosed player), **Pass Through When Enclosed** (on; `IsEnclosedTarget`) makes it fly straight through the cover to the player (`PursueTowards`/`FlyThrough`); turned off, enclosed players stay unreachable.
- Billboard pitch: EnemyPresentation's **Billboard Pitch** (on for the Manananggal, off for ground enemies) tilts WorldSprites to face each viewer's camera exactly (`FullBillboardRotation`, no roll), so a flyer above never looks flat. Like all billboarding it is computed locally on every peer from the networked position, so each player sees it facing them.
- [ManananggalBrain](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Enemies/Manananggal/ManananggalBrain.cs) (tuning in [ManananggalProfile](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Enemies/Manananggal/ManananggalProfile.cs), [Manananggal_Default](../Assets/PREFABS/Enemies/Profiles/Manananggal_Default.asset), **Create > Capstone > Enemies > Manananggal Profile**) has no home block or hearing. Its vision cone is pitched down by **Vision Pitch** (`EnemySenses.VisionPitch`, 50 degrees; 0 for other enemies). "Despawned" is a synced `hidden` flag: the network object stays alive but its sprite, blob shadow, body collider and fear source are off on every peer.
- Hunting: waits hidden (**First Pass Delay** 5-15 s, then **Respawn Delay** 15-40 s), warps outside one map edge (**Edge Margin** 12) at **Hunt Altitude** (14 m above the lowest block), reveals after **Reveal Delay** (0.5 s, so interpolation does not streak the sprite) and flies a straight line at **Hunt Speed** across the map to the opposite side, then hides again. Each pass picks a random heading (**Pass Direction Step**: 0 = any direction, 45 = edges and diagonals, 90 = map axes only) and a random parallel lane anywhere across the map's footprint, including along its edges, that crosses at least **Minimum Blocks Crossed** (1) street blocks (`ManananggalBrain.PlanLane`). Without a map it crosses its fallback area (**Fallback Pass Half Length**) on a random heading and lane.
- The first player it sees starts Chase: flies at that player (over obstacles) at **Chase Speed** for **Chase Duration** 20 s; each touch (**Attack Range**/**Attack Height**) deals **Contact Damage** 2 with its NetworkIdentity and hovers still for **Hit Pause Seconds** 2.5. Timeout, target death or boarding switch to Leaving: it flies at **Leave Speed** out of the map at hunt altitude (or after **Leave Timeout**), then Hunting waits the respawn delay again.
- [Manananggal_Sprites](../Assets/SPRITES/Enemies/Manananggal_Sprites.asset) uses the user's Left/Front/Right/back sheets (Manual, 4 frames per direction). The jumpscare front view and loading miniature currently use front-sheet frames as placeholders. Add [Manananggal.asset](../Assets/PREFABS/Enemies/Definitions/Manananggal.asset) to a MapTerminal destination's Enemy Pool to roll it; it is registered in SampleScene's spawn prefabs.
- [EnemySetupTests](../Assets/Tests/EditMode/EnemySetupTests.cs) check its wiring/profile/registration; [ManananggalTests](../Assets/Tests/PlayMode/ManananggalTests.cs) cover hidden waits, straight altitude passes and despawn, the downward cone (ahead/behind/range/roof), spotting during a pass, flying over a wall, reaching a player under a roof and one fully enclosed in a box, hits with pauses, and chase timeout to Leaving and Hunting. Live Steam behaviour is unverified.

## Round clock, travel time and midnight

- Premise: each round, players must sacrifice an agimat quota to the Albularyo at base before they run out of time (see Agimats and the Albularyo).
- [RoundClock](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Player/RoundClock.cs) sits on SampleScene's persistent NetworkManager object. It is server-authoritative and broadcasts a `RoundClockMessage` every **Sync Interval**; clients extrapolate between messages.
  - Settings: **Round Minutes** 45 real minutes for **Clock Hours** 12, so one hour is 3.75 minutes; **Low Time Hours** 3; **Base Scene Name** SampleScene; **Return Countdown Seconds** 30; **Left Behind Health** 2; **Game Over Seconds** 5.
  - The clock runs only away from base, never during travel or game over. It starts at noon and shows frame `elapsed hours mod 12`, so both noon and midnight show 12.
- Travel time: [TravelTimeManager](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Player/TravelTimeManager.cs), a root object in SampleScene, lists **Costs** (Scene Name plus clock **Hours**; user-tuned, StreetsTest was 1).
  - The round-trip cost is added when leaving base; returning to base costs nothing.
  - Trips that would reach midnight are refused: the confirmation shows the travel time, a warning and a disabled Yes button.
- Midnight away from base starts the return countdown.
  - Every jeepney [TravelInteractable](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Player/TravelInteractable.cs) away from base boards the player. Pressing E away from base before midnight also starts the same countdown.
  - Each player boards themselves. Players aboard are frozen and ignored by enemy senses and chases.
  - The jeepney leaves for base when every player has boarded or the countdown ends. Players who did not press E die when it leaves: health drops to 0 (enemies ignore them) and `ServerPlayerLeftBehind` fires, the hook for future inventory loss. They travel with the group while dead (`RoundClock.IsAwaitingRespawn`, also true for any dead player) and respawn at base spawn points with **Left Behind Health** 2 (one heart). Dead players cannot board.
- If every player is dead away from base for **All Dead Return Seconds** (4), `ServerAllPlayersDied` fires and the server sends everyone to base, where they respawn with one heart.
- With an [AgimatBank](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Player/AgimatBank.cs) present (SampleScene), rounds complete only by sacrificing the quota (`ServerCompleteRound`: elapsed resets, Round increments, `ServerRoundCompleted`); arriving at base after midnight just waits. The bank sets `RoundClock.QuotaReachable`; at base (not traveling), when no listed MapTerminal trip is affordable (`AnyTripAffordable`; without terminals, until midnight) and turned-in plus held agimats are below the quota, the server calls `ServerGameOver()`.
- Without a bank (legacy/tests), arriving at base after midnight checks `RoundClock.QuotaMet` (null counts as met):
  - Quota met: `ServerCompleteRound()`.
  - Quota not met: game over.
- Game over: GameOver locks controls and shows the HUD game over screen for Game Over Seconds. Then health becomes 6, stamina is restored (`PlayerStamina.ServerRestore`), players move to spawn points and the round resets to 1 (`ServerGameReset`, which also clears the agimat bank). The scene is not reloaded.
- HUD: [RoundClockHud](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Player/RoundClockHud.cs) on the [PlayerHud prefab](../Assets/PREFABS/PlayerHud.prefab) contains:
  - ClockPanel at the top right, with **Hour Sprites** in sheet order ClockUI-Sheet_0..11, where 0 is 12 o'clock. It blinks and pulses its scale while 3 or fewer hours remain (9 o'clock onwards).
  - CountdownPanel at the top centre.
  - GameOverPanel, a full-screen override canvas.
- Tests: [RoundClockSetupTests](../Assets/Tests/EditMode/RoundClockSetupTests.cs) cover frame and low-time math, texts, and scene/prefab wiring. [RoundClockTests](../Assets/Tests/PlayMode/RoundClockTests.cs) use an in-memory host to cover the paused base clock, cost deduction, refused trips, the countdown and boarding, the quota reset, the left-behind penalty, game over and the reset, enemies ignoring aboard/dead players, the all-dead return and the base-only travel map. Live Steam multi-client behaviour is unverified.

## Agimats and the Albularyo

- [AgimatBank](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Player/AgimatBank.cs) on SampleScene's persistent NetworkManager object (wired by SteamNetworkManager like RoundClock) holds one global inventory shared by all players: Gold, Silver and Bronze counts plus the round's turned-in count. Host-authoritative; every change broadcasts `AgimatStateMessage` (also sent to late joiners). Counts carry over rounds and scenes and clear only on the game reset. Currency use of the types is deferred; every agimat counts as 1 toward the quota.
- Quota: `AgimatBank.QuotaFor(round)` = 3 + 2^round (5, 7, 11, 19, 35...). Server code adds agimats with `ServerAdd(type, amount)` (pickups are not implemented yet; the component's context menu has debug adds). `ServerSacrifice(type)` moves one agimat to turned-in; reaching the quota resets turned-in to 0 and calls `RoundClock.ServerCompleteRound()` (timer reset, higher quota). Sacrifices are refused during game over or travel.
- [AlbularyoInteractable](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Player/AlbularyoInteractable.cs) (E, "Albularyo" near SampleScene's MapTerminal, Nametag "Talk to the Albularyo.") opens the local persistent [AlbularyoScreen](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Player/AlbularyoScreen.cs) ([prefab](../Assets/PREFABS/AlbularyoScreen.prefab), sorting 500). The NPC is a 2D billboard: its WorldSprites child (SpriteRenderer, SolidSprite.mat, scale 0.3 like players, placeholder art MaleFront.png) carries [BillboardSprite](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Player/BillboardSprite.cs) (local, upright toward the local player's camera, optional **Pitch**; use it for any static NPC/item sprite), the root has DistanceFadeSprite, and the invisible capsule collider on its Body child is what E/nametags aim at. Screen: top dialogue panel (blackstroke) with a **Portrait** Image on its left (the bust; placeholder MaleFront.png, preserve aspect: assign the real art on that Image) and a random line from [AlbularyoDialogue.asset](../Assets/Settings/AlbularyoDialogue.asset) ([AlbularyoDialogue](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Player/AlbularyoDialogue.cs), **Create > Capstone > Albularyo Dialogue**: **Request Lines** while agimats are needed, **Quota Met Lines** for **Quota Met Seconds** after the quota is met; placeholders {0} still needed, {1} quota, {2} turned in, {3} "agimat"/"agimats"; one line per visit, never the same twice in a row, or rotated every **Line Change Interval**), a larger offer panel with each type's icon, count and a Sacrifice button (disabled at 0, HoverRevealGraphic), bottom-left "Turned in: Nx" + agimat icon, bottom-right **Reward Label** "Reward: ???" (placeholder until currency), and Leave. Escape/Leave close it; it also closes on game over, travel or losing the local player. Buttons send `AgimatSacrificeRequest`; the host accepts only from living players within **Sacrifice Range** (6 m) of an Albularyo.
- While open it locks controls and hides the HUD through [HudVisibility](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Player/HudVisibility.cs) (static owner set like PlayerControlLock; always `Show` the same owner): PlayerHud health/stamina, RoundClockHud clock/countdown (the game over panel still shows) and the agimat column hide. New HUD readouts should respect `HudVisibility.Hidden`.
- HUD: [AgimatHud](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Player/AgimatHud.cs) on the PlayerHud prefab's **Agimats** panel (top-left below stamina, before DamageFlash) shows rows agimatgold/agimatsilver/agimatbronze "x0" and agimaticon "turnedIn/quota" (icons in [Assets/SPRITES/UI](../Assets/SPRITES/UI), blood_crow text).
- Tests: [AgimatSetupTests](../Assets/Tests/EditMode/AgimatSetupTests.cs) cover the quota sequence, HUD/screen/scene wiring and billboard pitch math; [AgimatTests](../Assets/Tests/PlayMode/AgimatTests.cs) use an in-memory host for HUD sync, the screen hiding the HUD, button sacrifices, completing a round, range rejection and the stuck-at-base game over and reset. Live Steam multi-client behaviour is unverified.

## Death, jumpscares and spectating

- [PlayerDeathScreen](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Player/PlayerDeathScreen.cs) is on the PlayerHud prefab's **DeathScreen** child (override canvas, sorting order 550: above DamageFlash 500, below GameOverPanel 600) with Blackout, Jumpscare and SpectatingLabel children. It is local only and reacts when the local player's health reaches 0: it locks controls (`PlayerControlLock`) and hides the player's first-person canvases.
- Creature kill: the screen turns black and the killer's front view zooms in (**Zoom Seconds**, **Zoom Start Scale**, **Hold Seconds**), then fades to black. The image comes from [EnemyJumpscare](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Player/EnemyJumpscare.cs) on the killer's prefab (**Front View** sprite, **Final Screen Height**, **Focus Point**), found from `PlayerHealth.KillerAssetId`. The Focus Point (0-1 from the sprite's bottom-left) becomes the image pivot, so it stays at the screen centre and the zoom closes in on it; its Inspector preview sets it by click/drag and outlines the final 16:9 view. Every new creature needs EnemyJumpscare with a front view and must pass its NetworkIdentity to `TakeDamage`. The Tikbalang uses the user's tikbalangjumpscare sprite, focused on the face (0.54, 0.85). Deaths without a killer (left behind) fade to black after **No Killer Delay** (1 s). Jumpscare SFX are deferred.
- After **Fade Seconds**/**Black Hold Seconds**, if others are alive the dead player's camera follows a living player's camera position, yaw and synced pitch (sorted by netId); `Player/SpectateNext` (left mouse) cycles. The watched player's and dead players' world sprites are hidden locally. It switches automatically when the target dies; with nobody alive it stays black until the server returns everyone to base. Respawning restores the camera, canvases and controls. Dead players' flashlights are off and they make no noise.
- [PlayerDeathScreenTests](../Assets/Tests/PlayMode/PlayerDeathScreenTests.cs) cover the jumpscare zoom, the no-killer delay, spectating/cycling/auto-switch, all dead and revival with an in-memory host. Live Steam behaviour is unverified.
